source_text: Post haec illud conatur incessere, quod nos apostoli Pauli testimonio comprobavimus, quia Deus hominem de seminibus operetur. Argumentaturque me fecisse fraudem, qui huic loco illa dicta voluerim coaptare, qua de frumentis prolata constabat; quasi ego aut ibi Apostoli sententiam, ut hic aestimat, dividuam fecerim, aut propter aliud testimonii recordatus sim quam ut eius finem monstrarem formatorem seminum omnium Deum credi oportere. Beatus enim Paulus postquam fidem resurrectionis, multiplicationis diurnae conciliavit exemplis; intulit quod universam naturam possit attingere, dicens: Deus autem illi dat corpus prout vult, et unicuique seminum proprium corpus; id est, omni semini corpus, quod proprietas eius reposcit, attribuit. Non ergo quod de frumentis dictum est, de homine volui intellegi; sed hoc quod dictum est, unicuique seminum proprium corpus a Deo auctore conferri, in destructionem vestram, quorum dogmate id negatur, arripui. Nequaquam igitur, sicut tu putas, supervacuo feci illius sententiae mentionem, nec ea fraudulenter, ut mentiris, sum abusus; nec tu de humanis seminibus hominem a Deo fieri, sicut peieras, credis; quod non opinando, sed fidem tuam intellegendo confirmo.
pass_a_gloss: After these things he tries to attack that which we proved by the testimony of the apostle Paul, that God works the human from seeds. And he argues that I made a fraud, who wanted to fit to this place those sayings which stood as brought forth about grains; as if I either made the Apostle's sentence divided there, as he estimates here, or remembered the testimony for another thing than that I might show its end, that God the former of all seeds ought to be believed. For blessed Paul after he conciliated the faith of resurrection by examples of daily multiplication; brought in what can touch the whole nature, saying: But God gives it a body as he wills, and to each of the seeds its own body; that is, he attributes to every seed the body which its property demands. Not therefore what was said about grains did I want understood about the human; but this which was said, that its own body is conferred on each of the seeds by God the author, I snatched for your destruction, by whose dogma that is denied. By no means therefore, as you think, did I make mention of that sentence superfluously, nor did I abusively, as you lie, use it; nor do you believe, as you perjure, that a human is made by God from human seeds; which I confirm not by opining but by understanding your faith.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself

pass_b_english: After this he tries to attack the point we established through the apostle Paul’s testimony: that God makes a human being from seed. He argues that I acted fraudulently by applying to this subject words admittedly spoken about grain. As though I had either broken the apostle’s statement in pieces there, as he imagines here, or recalled that testimony for any reason other than to demonstrate its conclusion: God must be believed to form every kind of seed. For after blessed Paul supported faith in the resurrection through examples of daily multiplication, he added something applicable to all nature: ‘But God gives it a body as he wills, and to each of the seeds its own body’ (1 Corinthians 15:38). That is, he assigns every seed the body its particular nature requires. I therefore did not intend words spoken about grain to be understood as about a human being. Rather, I seized upon the statement that God the maker gives each seed its own body to destroy your position, since your doctrine denies it. Therefore I certainly did not mention that statement needlessly, as you suppose, or use it fraudulently, as you falsely allege. Nor do you believe, despite your false oath, that God makes a human being from human seed. I affirm this not by conjecturing, but by understanding your creed.

Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.
Seed is God's work in generation; Julian refuses to make semen a vehicle of natural evil.
